comment: This is Rock City, the unofficial capital of show business.\n\tThis is the place for everything you will need to make it: record labels, concert venues, recording studios, song publishers, radio stations, etc.\n\tStart by clicking on the circular icon at the top of the screen to get to the Practice Room.

This moldy and smoke-smelling shack is where your band will be hanging out. Click on the gray boxes to hire musicians for your band.\n\tYou can have a minimum of one person to a max of five people in your band. The musicians are paid weekly and their pay demands are stated in the list.\n\tDon't forget to give the band a name (click Change Band Name).

Now <¤CBand.name> need a demo, but first you have to have a song. Go to a song publisher and purchase the license for a song.\n\tRock City has two song publishers: the independent Melody Publishing, which is open now, and Global Publishing, part of the powerful Global-concern, which will be available later in the game.

Time to record  choose a studio and get to it! There are several studios in Rock City, but only two are available at this point  the worn-down Garage Studio and the classic Strawberry Studios.\n\tMore will be available later in the game. The more skilled musicians you have, the better the result.

Welcome to the studio. Many a celebrity has spent hours here, smoking and waiting for the engineer to get the gear ready.\n\tPlay around with the gears and levers, try out some session musicians, and play around with your track.\n\tWhen you click OK, the demo is finished and can't be changed.

Are you ready to meet the Great White of the music industry  the record labels?\n\tAt this point, you can choose between the enthusiasts of Rebel Records or the missionaries of Rainbow Records.\n\tMore labels will be available later in the game.

Do a few live gigs to spawn interest with label execs. Rock City has five concert venues: the suburban Café Lizette, the rough Rock Pit, the elegant Mirror Ball, the classic Avenue and the spacious Palladium.\n\tOn top of that is the huge arena Colosseum, but you are far from playing there. Better start with one of the smaller venues.

In order to sell records, you'll need some PR. There's a lot of media in Rock City, from Radio FM and TV24 (available later in the game). Both can air your band's songs and videos, do interviews or whatever.
	The daily City News prints reviews and entertainment news, just like the music weekly Zer0 Magazine.
	There's also the Record Store. Buy adverts and give the reporters gifts to get your band some attention.
	Playing live is a good way to get an audience and Rock City has plenty of concert venues so get your hands dirty.
You can't release a record without a sleeve. Go to the Design Studio to create a record cover. As usual, the rule is the more money you spend, the better the result.

There are three charts to top. Radio FM has a list of the most played records every week, TV24 has the Viewers' Chart with the viewers' favourites, and Record Store has a list of this week's top sellers.\n\tCheck in to said buildings to contemplate the charts.
There's a Calendar to help you plan your strategy, see up-coming events, forecast your financial situation and  see how sales are doing.\n\tClick the date on top of the screen to go to the Calendar.
If you have trouble getting a label interested, you might want to try recording a different song or even change your band.
Should you need money, you can ask the label for an advance.\n\tHowever, they won't give advances without getting something in return. Anything you get, you'll have to pay back in sales.
